jobs.title: AI GTM Program Manager
jobs.description:
Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization
.We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire
customer journey.

We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses.
We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey.
We're designing the future of autonomous marketing, taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do.

And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi
— so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.

Bloomreach
builds agentic AI systems for our customers. We also run them ourselves.

Our AI SDR program books sales meetings with AI - inbound and outbound, across four regions, in multiple languages. The program needs an owner: someone who sets its direction, drives its results, and proves its ROI. This is a program leadership role, not an engineering one. Two dedicated AI ops experts build and run the platform. You decide what it does, why, and for whom. You should understand AI agents well enough to direct the people building them - your leverage is judgment, but being tech savvy is a must.

The team experiments by default: we test new AI tools, run scoped POCs, and keep what works. You'll own the program, its direction, its results, its pipeline number.

What You'll Own

The AI SDR program, end to end. Inbound and outbound, AMER + EMEA + APAC. Who gets enrolled, what the agents say, when a human takes over, and what it produces in pipeline. You set direction; the platform ops managers make it run. (Inbound request ops and routing sit with a colleague.)
Pipeline as your number, ROI as your story. Meetings booked → accepted → qualified pipeline created. Cost per meeting, cost per pipeline dollar. You report the program's return to leadership, with numbers that hold up under questioning.
The human SDR side. SDRs are the other half of the program - and where it most often breaks: lead quality disputes, unclear prioritization, follow-up that dies after one touch, handovers that lose context. You'll sit with the SDR teams and their leaders, find root causes, and fix them - with an AI assist, a process change, or a better definition.
The human–agent split. What agents do, what humans do, and where the handover sits. You own that line and move it based on evidence.
Signal-driven enrollment. Targeting runs on manual batches today. You'll drive the move to continuous enrollment based on account scoring, intent signals, and engagement decay. You define the logic; the ops team builds it.
The buying experience. Outreach should arrive because an account signalled something, say something true about the buyer's business, and make the next step obvious.
Program reporting. Volume, coverage, results, and ROI on a live dashboard, generated automatically. Parts still run on exports. Fix that early.
What comes next. The AI SDR pattern - signal in, agent acts, human closes - applies beyond outbound: event follow-up, hand-raiser nurture, re-engagement. Once the core program runs well, you'll make the case for the next one and drive its launch.

What success looks like after 3 months

Outbound volume and coverage are consistent across regions. Nobody asks "why did outbound drop last week?"
Leadership references your ROI model in planning: cost per meeting, cost per pipeline dollar, trend.
The top three SDR pain points from your first quarter are root-caused and fixed - and SDR leaders would confirm it unprompted.
Meeting acceptance is high. Rejections have known causes, not theories.
Reporting is fully automated. Your time goes into decisions.
The program activities and volume is connected to human activities, pipeline number for ICP accounts is bigger - and you can show which changes drove it.
At least one new agentic program is live and producing pipeline.

What you'll bring

You've run programs with a number attached. Demand gen, SDR/BDR, growth, or GTM programs where you owned the outcome and defended the metric.
You've operated AI workflows in production. You've deployed, directed, or owned automations other people depended on. You can set requirements, challenge the build, and tell when the agent is the problem versus the data. You don't need to write code - you do need to never be bluffed by it.
ROI fluency. You can build a cost-per-outcome model and explain it. You'd rather show a live dashboard than a slide.
You diagnose team problems at the source. "The leads are bad" is where your investigation starts, not where it ends. You've worked with frontline teams, found the real constraint, and fixed it.
SDRs, AEs, and their leaders are your users. When the program misfires, you’ll be their point of contact.
The buyer's point of view. Buyers don't care that outreach was efficient - only that it was worth their time. You'll kill a volume that doesn't clear that bar.
Enough technical depth to be dangerous. You can read a workflow, question a data model, and learn a new tool in a week. Experience with our stack is welcome, not required.
Global comfort. Four regions, several languages, overlap with US hours.

Big Advantage:: hands-on LLM tooling beyond vendor UIs (Claude Code, MCP, custom agents); time in or working with SDR/BDR and demand gen function in B2B SaaS.

The stack you'll drive

Salesforce

Qualified
Salesloft
UserGems
Claude - plus a mandate to evaluate AI-native tooling with a clear bar for measurable impact.

The team

You'll join Marketing Operations six people who operationalize and automate everything in marketing. Two of them work full-time on the AI SDR platform: they build and run it; you set its direction and co-own it: reporting and attribution, co-own and maintain inbound/outbound processes and find new tools. It's a team that builds its own tools rather than filing tickets for them.

Culture:

As a Lead Data Analyst, you’ll play a central role in shaping how Admiral uses customer data to deliver smarter, more connected and more personalised customer experiences across UK Customer.

We’re investing in Adobe Experience Platform, Customer Journey Analytics and Adobe Journey Optimiser to transform how we understand customer behaviour, build audiences and activate personalisation across our digital and marketing channels. This role will help turn that ambition into reality, creating the data foundations, audience strategy and governance needed to make Adobe a trusted, scalable capability across the business.

You’ll own the logical design of customer data models and audiences within Adobe Experience Platform, ensuring schemas, datasets and audience definitions are structured, reusable and easy to understand. Working closely with Digital, Marketing, Data Privacy and the wider Digital Analytics team, you’ll translate business goals into clear data and audience designs that support better measurement, better decision-making and more relevant customer journeys.

By embedding strong governance from the start, you’ll help ensure our customer data is not only powerful, but trusted, explainable and used responsibly enabling UK Customer to move faster, personalise more effectively and build more consistent experiences across channels.

The Role

Define and govern XDM schema and dataset standards, ensuring consistency and analytical clarity across Adobe Experience Platform.
Translate business requirements into clear, logical audience definitions and validate behaviour, scale and eligibility.
Work closely with our Digital Analytics and Marketing teams to advise on how audiences should be used for activation and measurement.
Own the definition of any audiences that we export to third party tools, e.g. for optimisation of paid media.
Establish shared analytical taxonomies and attributes used across journeys, reporting and experimentation.
Work in liaison with Data Privacy and Martech to ensure data labels are applied appropriately on the platform for data and marketing restriction.

Essential Skills & Experience

Experience designing and governing audiences within Adobe Experience Platform, Real-Time CDP or equivalent environments.
Understanding of XDM concepts, including event vs profile modelling and schema-driven design.
Hands-on experience working with Customer Journey Analytics (CJA) or equivalent journey analytics tooling.
Understanding of how audiences are consumed by Adobe Journey Optimizer (AJO), Adobe Target and downstream activation platforms.
Experience incorporating privacy and consent considerations into audience and schema design to support responsible data use.

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

Black Lotus Labs has an opening for a Senior Lead Security Engineer that will leverage Lumen’s unique visibility to hunt, investigate, and scale discovery of evolving malicious threats, provide mission-relevant intelligence, and support mitigations on large networks. Our global visibility into one of the world’s largest and most interconnected IP backbones, combined with our computing cluster and analytic platforms, presents exciting opportunities to integrate machine learning, graph analytics, automation, and approved AI-enabled tools as we find new ways to hunt for threats across the internet. Black Lotus Labs has detected and disrupted key evolving threats at an internet scale for years.

This position will work alongside Black Lotus Labs advanced security researchers, data engineers, malware reverse engineers, data scientists, and our customers to tackle evolving threats accelerated by technologies like our Hadoop ecosystem (HBase, HDFS, Spark, Kafka, AirFlow), Elasticsearch and Redis clusters, Docker using Docker Swarm, malware environment, a network of honeypots, and modern AI-assisted research and development capabilities.

This is a close-knit, experienced, amazingly smart team that you can be a part of and help build out.

This position requires an active TS/SCI security clearance w/ CI Poly.

Location

This is a remote position with office visits in Herndon, VA approximately 2 times per month.

The Main Responsibilities

Research latest threat attacker tools, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) with a goal of automating detection.
Work with cyber operators, when requested, to conduct in-depth investigations on cyber threat activity and provide mitigation guidance.
Automate investigations through Python scripting and data analysis using visualization in Jupyter Notebooks and Grafana
Build and maintain trust relationships with other intelligence teams, law enforcement, and other outside groups.
Support customer RFIs on incidents and emerging threats.
Use approved AI-enabled tools to accelerate research, coding, data exploration, documentation, and knowledge discovery while validating outputs through independent analytical judgment.
Develop repeatable workflows that combine analyst expertise, automation, and AI-assisted capabilities to improve investigative efficiency and analytical quality.

What We Look For In a Candidate

Candidates must effectively communicate complex domain-specific concepts, ensuring clarity for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Familiarity with adversary capabilities, infrastructure, and techniques that can be applied in collaboration with supporting teams and partners to discover, track, and defend against the adversaries aggression towards customer networks.
Experience using OSINT methods for investigation, including discovering novel threats in malware repositories.
Scripting experience with Python and familiarity with distributed computing.
Extensive experience hunting threat actors and developing algorithms and techniques to identify new threats from large data sets.
Deep knowledge of network-based threats and identifying behaviors without attack payloads.
Strong analytical thinking and ability to quickly pick up new methods, tools and programming languages.
User-level experience in a Unix-based environment.
Familiarity with extracting data through SQL.
Strong writing skills to assist in sharing our knowledge with the public.
Demonstrable knowledge of several of the following areas: cybersecurity concepts, network protocols, firewalls, IDS/IPS systems, cyber threat hunting, malware analysis tools and techniques, cyber threat intelligence, common threat actor TTPs, application security concepts, cloud security fundamentals.
Ability to rapidly develop proficiency in unfamiliar technical domains through foundational analytical skills, self-directed learning, and effective use of AI-assisted research and problem-solving tools.
Ability to use AI-enabled tools responsibly to augment technical research, analysis, coding, documentation, and report development while maintaining professional skepticism and analytical rigor.

jobs.title: Junior Research Analyst
jobs.description:
We are adding a Junior Research Analyst to our team to support a large scale engagement with a major financial services provider. This role is essential for keeping our advisory work grounded in facts and clear records. As a fully remote position, you will work alongside our consultants to help translate complex management discussions into simple, actionable information that a leadership team can use every day.

About the role

The Junior Research Analyst exists to help our advisory practice stay organized and focused. In many large organizations, information gets lost in long email chains or forgotten after a meeting ends. You will help prevent this by acting as the project memory. Your work ensures that when we give advice to a client, it is based on a solid understanding of how their teams actually operate.
This is an entry level role where you will learn to look at the structural habits of a business. You will spend your time gathering data, observing how decisions are made, and turning those observations into clear written notes. The goal is not to produce hundreds of pages of analysis, but to find the few specific details that explain why a project is stalling or why a team feels stuck. You will be helping us make management easier for our clients by providing them with a quiet, reliable record of their own progress.

What you will do
Participate in remote calls and interviews to capture decisions, open questions, and specific handoffs between teams.
Turn raw notes and recordings into concise summaries that highlight the most important themes.
Review internal client documents to map out how information currently flows from one department to another.
Help maintain a centralized project record so that every team member knows what was decided and who owns the next step.
Conduct basic research into management structures and meeting rhythms to provide context for our recommendations.
Assist in the preparation of briefing materials that help our consultants stay informed before client sessions.
Identify recurring issues in client data, such as meeting overlaps or unclear reporting lines, and summarize them clearly.
Update project trackers and documentation regularly to ensure all information is current and accurate.

What we are looking for
A direct and plain writing style. You should be able to explain a complex situation without using corporate jargon or fluff.
Excellent attention to detail. You notice when a small detail in a meeting contradicts an earlier decision.
Strong organizational habits. You enjoy creating order out of messy information and keeping documents tidy.
A calm and steady approach to tasks. You can focus on quiet work and take the time needed to get a summary right.
Willingness to learn. You are curious about how businesses work and how people collaborate in a professional setting.
Reliability in a remote setting. You are comfortable managing your own schedule and meeting deadlines without being chased.
A preference for clarity. You would rather ask a clarifying question than guess at what a client meant.

Helpful background
Basic familiarity with document editors and spreadsheet tools for organizing lists and notes.
Previous experience in an internship or a part time role that required careful record keeping or reporting.
Educational background in business, social sciences, communications, or a related field where writing was a primary focus.
Experience summarizing long texts or discussions into brief, understandable points.
Comfort using remote communication tools to stay in touch with a distributed team throughout the day.

What we offer

This is a permanent, full time position that is conducted entirely remotely. We offer a competitive salary that is attractive for an entry level research role and reflects the value you bring to our team. You will have the opportunity to learn a practical, no nonsense approach to consulting that focuses on helping people work better together. We value quiet focus, clear writing, and a healthy work life balance that respects your time outside of work hours.

About Olive Tree Consulting

Olive Tree Consulting Group is a focused advisory practice that helps leadership teams solve recurring management issues. We typically work on the space between strategy and daily execution. A team can have very capable people and still find that decisions keep reopening, priorities stall, or responsibility remains unclear. These are rarely personality problems; they are structural habits that have not kept up with the company growth.
We favor practical changes over large scale transformation programs. Our work involves looking at how decisions are made, how meetings are run, and how ownership is recorded. We prefer useful written notes and clear ownership over polished presentations and vague alignment. Good advisory work should make things plainer and leave the team with a rhythm they can continue on their own.
The firm is built on the principle that memory is not a management system. We help teams create the smallest possible written record to support their work so that important follow up does not depend on who was in the room or who has the best memory. The goal is a quieter management pattern that makes the existing work easier to lead.

jobs.title: Nordic Corporate Security Manager
jobs.description:
Shape the future of security across the Nordics in a fast-growing, international business.

Verisure is seeking a highly experienced, strategic and hands-on Nordic Corporate Security Manager to lead and develop our physical security agenda across the Nordic region. This is a critical role with high visibility, supporting senior leadership and enabling continued growth in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

This is a rare opportunity to step into a high-growth, high-performing and profitable business with a clear mission: to protect what matters most.
Verisure operates in a category with remarkably low market penetration, offering fast potential for expansion. Our growth is rapid, resilient, and highly profitable — powered by a recurring revenue model and deep, long-term customer relationships. What sets Verisure apart is the strength of our platform: a robust, scalable operating model and a high-performing culture rooted in purpose. We’re growing fast, we’re doing it right — and we’re still just getting started.

About Verisure

Verisure is the leading provider of professionally monitored security services with 24/7 response in Europe and Latin America.
Every day, our dedicated teams use leading technology to Deter, Detect, Verify and Intervene to protect our residential and small business customers against intrusion, burglary, fires, physical attack, home occupation, theft from a business, life-threatening emergencies and other hazards that may risk the safety, wellbeing or condition of our customers and their properties.

We protect a portfolio of over 6.3 million customers across 18 countries.
In 14 of our 18 geographies, we lead the category in terms of customers served and we continue to gain market share. We have a strong track record of profitable and resilient growth, primarily delivered organically by our codified and industrialised business model with high share of recurring revenues (about 90%) and industry leading retention.

Our mission is to give our customers peace of mind by protecting what matters most to them. We believe that everyone has the right to feel safe and secure.

For the year ended 31 December 2025, Verisure delivered another year of strong, profitable growth, generating €3.7 billion in Total Revenue, €1.7 billion in Adjusted EBITDA (46% margin) and €953 million in Adjusted EBIT (25% margin). For more information:  www.verisure.com

Verisure in the Nordics

Born in Sweden over 35 years ago, Verisure has grown from a local pioneer into the leading provider of monitored security solutions across the Nordic region and globally.
Today, Sweden stands as our third largest market and Norway as our fifth, with Denmark and Finland playing critical strategic roles in our portfolio. All four countries have delivered exceptional growth over the past five years and hold #1 positions in their respective markets.

With more than 2,000 passionate colleagues and partners across the Nordics, we proudly protect homes and small businesses every day.
As we continue to scale and accelerate, strengthening our brand, reputation, and trust with customers, communities, and key stakeholders is essential. Our ambition is clear: to make the Nordics the most recognized and most preferred security provider in the region.

Responsibilities Of The Corporate Security Manager

As Nordic Security Manager, you hold full accountability for the Corporate Security function across the Nordic region, with a clear mandate to lead, shape, and continuously strengthen the overall security framework
. You are expected to define and drive the regional security strategy, ensuring it is not only aligned with global standards but also effectively translated into concrete actions, measurable outcomes, and consistent execution across all Nordic markets.

In this role, you are not only responsible for setting direction—you are expected to ensure delivery, follow-through, and tangible impact
. You will proactively identify risks, challenge existing ways of working, and implement robust frameworks that enhance resilience, protect critical assets, and support the business in achieving its strategic objectives.

You will operate in a highly cross-functional environment, working closely with senior stakeholders across Legal, HR, Technology, Information Security, and Compliance. As a trusted partner, you are expected to influence decision-making at a senior level, provide clear and actionable insights, and ensure that security is embedded into business processes rather than treated as a standalone function
. In parallel, you will collaborate with international peers and Group functions to drive consistency, share best practices, and contribute to the continuous evolution of the global security agenda.

Success in this role requires the ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on involvement
, taking ownership in critical situations while maintaining a long-term, proactive perspective on risk and security development.

Core responsibilities

Develop and implement the corporate and physical security strategy across the Nordic region, ensuring a consistent level of security maturity across all markets to protect Verisure’s people, facilities, assets, operations, information, reputation, service continuity, and customer trust against risks of any nature
Identify risks, gaps, threats, and vulnerabilities, and drive preventive, reactive, and predictive mitigation actions
Lead internal investigations focused on the detection and prevention of misconduct fraud, loss of sensitive information, illegal competition, and other security-related irregularities
Address internal and external incidents with potential legal, operational, financial, or reputational impact, ensuring appropriate investigation, escalation, documentation, and follow-through
Collaborate with HR, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Technology, and Information Security to gather relevant evidence, support sensitive investigations, and ensure actions are aligned with company policies and applicable requirements
Coordinate, where appropriate, with law enforcement, public authorities, external advisors, and relevant security bodies in connection with incidents or investigations
Develop preventive and predictive methodologies to strengthen fraud deterrence, crime prevention, and loss prevention across the region
Monitor compliance with security policies, procedures, standards, and governance requirements, including alignment with global standards and regulatory expectations
Promote employee awareness, responsible behaviours, and a strong security and compliance culture across the Nordics
Lead corporate security initiatives, including insider risk, personnel security, physical security, crime prevention, fraud deterrence, and investigations
Prevent, detect, manage, and learn from security incidents with potential operational, legal, financial, or reputational impact
Own and continuously improve incident management processes, tools, reporting routines, and governance across the region
Provide intelligence, analysis, and actionable insights related to incidents, investigations, risks, and emerging threats to support strategic decision-making
Define, track, and report security KPIs and continuous improvement metrics, including investigation, fraud, incident, and resilience indicators
Own and develop the Nordic Business Continuity Planning framework, ensuring readiness to protect critical services and recover effectively from disruption
Lead crisis management processes, coordination, exercises, and continuous improvement, ensuring the organisation can respond with structure, speed, and discipline
Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership across the Nordics, translating complex security risks into clear, pragmatic, and business-oriented recommendations
Collaborate with Group and regional security leaders to share best practices, drive consistency, and contribute to the evolution of Verisure’s broader security agenda
Contribute to enterprise risk management, organisational resilience, and the safe development of the business across the Nordic region

Candidate profile

You are a highly seasoned and trusted security leader with the ability to operate confidently at both strategic and operational levels in a complex, international environment. With a strong track record of leading security functions across multiple countries, you bring deep expertise across corporate security, physical security, personnel security, fraud deterrence, investigations, business continuity, crisis management, and organisational resilience.

You understand that security is not only about protecting the business from risk, but also about enabling the business to grow in a safe, trusted, and disciplined way. You have a well-developed business mindset and understand how to balance risk, operational needs, customer trust, reputation, and commercial priorities, while maintaining the highest standards of integrity and professionalism. You are a natural influencer who builds credibility quickly with senior stakeholders and can translate complex security risks into clear, actionable business decisions. Known for your sound judgment and discretion, you are comfortable handling sensitive matters, working with confidential information, and navigating high-pressure situations with calm, structure, and follow-through. You combine analytical depth with a strong execution mindset and have a proven ability to develop preventive and predictive approaches, implement frameworks, lead investigations, manage incidents, and continuously strengthen security maturity across markets.

Experience And Qualifications

10–15+ years of progressive experience within Corporate Security, Risk Management, Intelligence, Investigations, Fraud Prevention, or a related field
Solid background in corporate security, physical security, personnel security, investigations, fraud deterrence, and protection of sensitive information
Proven experience leading security across multiple countries, preferably in a multinational organisation
Strong experience working in matrixed and complex organisational structures, with the ability to align Group, regional, and local stakeholders
Demonstrated experience in incident management, crisis response, business continuity planning, and organisational resilience
Experience designing and implementing preventive, reactive, and predictive security measures to reduce risk and protect reputation, service continuity, and critical assets
Experience leading sensitive internal investigations and collaborating with HR, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Technology, Information Security, external advisors, and authorities where relevant
Strong understanding of investigation methodology, evidence gathering, incident documentation, root-cause analysis, and follow-up governance
Experience developing and monitoring security KPIs, incident management tools, fraud indicators, and continuous improvement metrics
Experience engaging with and advising senior leadership and executive stakeholders on complex, sensitive, and high-impact matters
Strong understanding of risk management frameworks, compliance requirements, governance processes, and international standards such as ISO
A proven ability to develop strategy and translate it into actionable plans, operational routines, measurable outcomes, and sustained behavioural change
Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and driving alignment across multiple stakeholders, markets, and functions
High level of integrity, discretion, and professional judgment, with the ability to handle sensitive and confidential information
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail, structure, and an ability to separate signal from noise in complex situations
Ability to operate effectively under pressure and in crisis situations, while maintaining clarity, calm, and disciplined execution

jobs.title: Program Manager, Harmful Activity
jobs.description:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge.  Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.
ABOUT THE ROLE: We serve our community of users and customers by working tirelessly to preserve free expression and choice, create limitless interactivity, and maintain a safe digital marketplace. The Safety Integrity Program Manager, Harmful Activity will drive priorities, measures, and system health for harmful activity, owning program standards and execution across upstream systems and downstream operations.
You are an experienced program manager with a strong background in content integrity, abuse, or risk programs at scale. You are skilled at setting requirements for detection and automation, translating policy and legal constraints into practical workflows and controls, and driving cross-functional partners to improve coverage, precision, and enforcement quality. You thrive in fast-paced environments and excel at turning operational signals into lasting improvements.
RESPONSIBILITIES: Drive priorities, measures, and system health for harmful activity, and continuously improve execution
Set requirements and success criteria for detection and automation, and drive Product, Engineering, and Operations to improve coverage, precision, and enforcement quality at scale.
Translate legal, policy, and technical constraints into practical requirements, workflows, controls, and escalation paths for Product, Engineering, and Operations.
Identify gaps in the current framework and drive enhancements to policies, procedures, controls, and workflows.
Own escalations, quality assurance, and complex case patterns for residual volume, and use those signals to harden standards and automation over time.
Align and drive Product, Engineering, Policy, Legal, and Operations partners to resolve dependencies, make decisions, and move critical work forward with clear accountable ownership.
Build and maintain the documentation, guidance, and operating standards that embed consistent execution across the program.
Monitor relevant regulatory developments, assess impact on the program, and ensure requirements stay accurate and executable.
Track and report operational performance, risks, and improvement opportunities with clear recommendations for leadership.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 5+ years in content integrity, safety operations, abuse operations, or related program roles supporting enforcement or risk programs at scale.
Experience owning or supporting program priorities, measures, and operational health for content or risk domains.
Working knowledge of harmful activity domains and how policy, legal, and technical constraints shape response.
Experience translating policy or legal requirements into practical workflows, controls, and escalation paths.
Experience working with automated or model-driven enforcement systems, including detection, classifiers, or policy automation.
Proven ability to drive cross-functional work with Product, Engineering, Policy, Legal, and Operations partners.
Strong analytical skills with experience using operational data to identify gaps, prioritize interventions, and track outcomes.
Clear written and verbal communication; able to brief leadership and document standards, decisions, and recommendations.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: Direct experience with harmful activity, integrity, or abuse programs at scale.
Experience setting requirements for detection, classifiers, or automation and partnering with Product or Engineering teams on outcomes.
Experience owning escalations, quality assurance, or residual case handling for enforcement programs.
Experience converting operational signals into product, process, or policy changes.
Exposure to integrity risks involving synthetic content, model misuse, or scaled manipulation.
Experience improving operating standards, documentation, and controls in a live program environment.
Background in high-scale consumer platforms, marketplaces, or technology products.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
$110,000 - $145,000 USD
Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at xAI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:
To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here. 

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Staff Technical Product & Program Manager, Security
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.

The mission of Aurora’s OneTech Security Product Management team is to embed security into every aspect of Aurora’s products—spanning software, hardware, and services. As a Staff Technical Product &Program Manager, Security
, you will be responsible for driving security strategy and initiatives across the organization, ensuring that security is a fundamental and functional part of the Aurora product development process.

You will act as a bridge between Security and Product teams across the organization, moving seamlessly between high-level strategy and detailed execution to ensure that complex, cross-functional security is successfully integrated into products developed across the company. Your ability to lead, influence, and manage large-scale security initiatives will be essential in safeguarding Aurora’s products and ensuring they meet the highest security standards.

The job level is negotiable based on experience. Flexible work locations are available (MTV, SFO, PIT, SEA, DET) for US-based employees (Full remote is not available for this role).

In this role, you will

Collaborate with product teams: Work closely with product management, Software and Hardware Development, engineering, and security teams to define security features, assess product risks, prioritize security initiatives, create business and technical use cases, and implement strategic controls that protect both product integrity and user trust.
Engage with suppliers and development partners: Work closely with hardware and software suppliers and Tier1 development partners to define and align on cybersecurity features, drive their timely delivery, and ensure that contributions meet Aurora’s security standards and support overall product integrity and user trust.
Develop high-level security roadmap(s): Work closely with product and engineering leads to develop high level roadmaps and plans (Business and Technical) which will highlight and document cross-functional dependencies as well as the critical path(s) of various programs and projects.
Lead security integration: Develop and execute security assurance, governance, and risk management programs, ensuring they are deeply embedded into all phases of product development from hardware to support applications and that they are aligned with company goals objectives.
Monitor and report: Define and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) related to product and security risks, ensuring transparency and data-driven decision-making across the organization.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in Technical Product, Program or Product Management role, in the automotive or AV domain preferred and also cybersecurity experience.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a STEM field or equivalent experience.
Proven experience developing product strategies, building product use cases, leading large-scale programs with an emphasis on project management, requirements management, and integrating hardware and software features into complex products.
Strong communication and leadership skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate with cross-functional product teams.
Hands-on experience participating and directing product development.

Desirable Qualifications

Experience building and scaling product programs from the ground up, particularly in product-focused environments or industries with stringent security requirements.
Strong knowledge of auto industry security standards and regulations (e.g. ISO21434)
Proven ability to lead broad organizational changes.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex security concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, particularly in a product context.
Advanced certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or equivalent

For roles based in San Francisco, CA, Mountain View, CA, and Seattle, WA: The salary range for this position is $181,000 - $262,000 per year.

For roles based in Pittsburgh, PA: The salary range for this position is $163,000 - $236,000 per year.

Aurora’s pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, relevant education or training, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future. The successful candidate will also be eligible for an annual bonus, equity compensation, and benefits.

Working at Aurora

At Aurora, we bring together extraordinarily talented and experienced people united by the strength of our values. We operate with integrity, set outrageous goals, and build a culture where we win together — all without any jerks.

We believe in-person work increases collaboration, empathy and our ability to lead effectively. As a result, we operate in a hybrid work environment where Aurorans are in office at least 3 days per week.

Our Careers page provides insight into what it is like to work at Aurora, and you can find all the latest updates in our Newsroom.

Our commitment to safety

At the core of everything we do is our commitment to safety. Building best-in-class self-driving technology will take time, and we believe that each employee at Aurora has a role in contributing to safety, every step of the way. Aurora expects commitment to our safety policies from every employee, and seeks candidates who take an active responsibility, can contribute to building an atmosphere of trust, and invest in the organization’s long-term success by prioritizing working safely, no matter what.

Our commitment to inclusion

Aurora considers candidates without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy status, parent or caregiver status, ancestry, political affiliation, veteran and/or military status, physical or mental disability, or any other status protected by federal or state law. Aurora considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at careersiteaccommodations@aurora.tech.

For California applicants, information collected and processed as part of your application and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Aurora’s California Employment Privacy Policy.

jobs.description:
Description

Do you want to be part of a global team that relentlessly pursues procurement excellence, improves operational processes and outcomes, and manages compliance and business risks? Do you have a solid procurement background, excel at program and stakeholder management, and thrive in a fast-paced environment?

We are hiring a Program Manager - Procurement Excellence to work closely with procurement stakeholders, operations, functions, systems and engineering to enable scalable, well-controlled business processes and decision-making.

This role sits within a broader team of program managers that operates as highly embedded business partners to procurement, focused on operational effectiveness and impact, scalable mechanisms, and risk-informed execution.

The ideal candidate combines strong business process thinking, stakeholder influence, operational rigor, and technical literacy to help teams move quickly while maintaining appropriate risk and control standards.

The ideal candidate require a high tolerance of ambiguity aligned to AWS Day 1 culture, ability to influence executive decisions, drive strategic initiatives and change management that deliver meaningful programmatic improvements.

This is not a traditional audit or policy-focused role. We designed this role for individuals who enjoy solving operational problems, driving influence and alignment across teams, and building scalable mechanisms in fast-paced environments. Over time, this role has opportunity to evolve toward broader technical program management style leadership responsibilities.

Your Role

Business Partnership & Operational Enablement

Partner closely with Technical, Engineering, Operations, Procurement, and Risk stakeholders to shape scalable business processes and controls.
Engage early with teams to influence decisions, identify risks, and enable efficient execution.
Translate risk and controls requirements into practical, actionable operating mechanisms.

Risk & Controls Integration

Design and improve scalable controls, guardrails, and operational frameworks that support business velocity while managing risk appropriately.
Simplify and modernize existing processes to align with evolving business needs and risk appetite.
Ensure controls are operationally practical and embedded into day-to-day workflows.

Business Process & Mechanism Ownership

Identify process gaps, friction points, and operational inefficiencies across programs and workflows.
Build mechanisms, playbooks, decision frameworks, and scalable patterns that improve consistency and reduce ambiguity.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives across governance, operational readiness, and execution processes.

Cross-Functional Coordination & Audit Readiness

Act as a business partner to Procurement teams and a key coordination point across Risk, Audit, Assurance, Legal, Technical and Engineering teams.
Streamline audit readiness and evidence gathering through scalable operational processes rather than manual coordination.
Ensure teams have clarity on ownership, expectations, and escalation paths.

Technical & Operational Collaboration

Engage effectively with technical teams by understanding system architecture, workflows, dependencies, and operational trade-offs.
Partner with engineering teams to ensure controls and operational requirements are designed into solutions early.
Use data and operational signals to identify risks, trends, and improvement opportunities.

What Good Looks Like For This Role

Procurement teams and functional partners proactively engage you as a trusted partner early in planning and execution.
Decisions move faster because of your involvement, not slower.
Processes become simpler, clearer, and more scalable over time.
Risk Management and controls are embedded into operational workflows rather than managed as separate activities.
Stakeholders experience clear ownership, practical guidance, and streamlined engagement across governance functions.

What We Are Not Looking For

Purely policy or checklist-driven approaches.
Candidates who operate primarily through approvals or gatekeeping or arm's length approach
Candidates who identify problems without driving practical solutions.

High stakeholder engagement, influencing and cross-functional ownership is essential is for the role.

The Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG) function is part of Amazon Infrastructure Services (AIS)

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities

Lead various audit programs, risk remediation, policy and process improvement projects internally and with external stakeholders
Take lead in establishing necessary controls, mechanisms, and policies to improve DCSP compliance and assurance
Drive culture of innovation, simplification and continuous improvement through best practice sharing, advocacy and hands-on leadership and execution of projects
Identify new tools and business processes that simplify, standardize and enable operational excellence
Derive actionable insights and routinely present recommendations from analysis

A day in the life

This role has a global scope so there is no standard day - there is much variety in the day
You could be starting with a morning meeting speaking with US team members, a coffee with APAC and finish up with a call with EMEA
You will work on multiple projects with global teams, stakeholders and customers
Your biggest customers will be our Data Center Services Procurement teams and our AWS security assurance teams. Stakeholders also include legal, finance, H&S and other Data Center Communities colleagues

About The Team

Data Center Procurement Governance (DCPG) is a global function that includes:

Program Management - a team of Program Managers who are strong business partners to procurement, intersect business process with technology and tooling across the procurement life cycle, to identify, architect and deliver impact projects for our DC procurement teams.

Procurement Systems, Tools & Analytics - Define, support and drive procurement technical roadmap in systems, tooling, automation, analytics and GenAI.

About AWS

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of program or project management experience
3+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
Bachelor's degree
Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
3+ years of driving process improvements experience
Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
Experience building processes, project management, and schedules

jobs.description:
Job Description

The HR Risk Operations Project Manager is responsible for leading complex HR risk, compliance, and operational programs from strategy through execution. This role partners closely with People Experience, Legal, Compliance, HRIS, Payroll, Finance, and business stakeholders to translate regulatory requirements, policy priorities, and operational risks into practical programs, standard operating procedures, tools, controls, reporting, and stakeholder guidance. The Manager serves as a consultative resource on employment policy and HR compliance matters, providing clear recommendations, drafting policy-related materials, and supporting consistent, defensible decision-making across the organization.

This role requires strong project and program management discipline, including the ability to develop project plans, manage timelines, coordinate cross-functional workstreams, identify dependencies and risks, and drive deliverables to completion in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. The ideal candidate will bring strong data analytics capabilities, including experience analyzing workforce data, identifying trends and risk indicators, building dashboards or tracking tools, and translating data into executive-ready insights and recommendations.

The HR Risk Operations Project Manager serves as a key member of the People & Culture team in support of firm-wide goals and objectives. This role will report to the Associate Director of HR Risk Operations.

Key responsibilities:

HR Regulatory Program Management

Lead complex HR risk, compliance, and operational programs from planning through execution, including project plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and deliverables.
Translate legal, regulatory, and business requirements into scalable HR processes, controls, communications, training materials, and stakeholder guidance.
Coordinate cross-functional workstreams by aligning stakeholders, clarifying roles and responsibilities, documenting decisions, and ensuring timely follow-through.
Manage large-scale HR programs supporting multinational firms on the Grant Thornton platform, integrations, and business optimization initiatives.
Support firmwide compliance initiatives, including workforce analysis, Respect in the Workplace training, compliance questionnaires, and other high-priority or confidential projects in partnership with P&C and Legal.
Oversee the firmwide Affirmative Action program, including OFCCP audit response, vendor management, reporting, and program governance.

HR Risk Operations

Partner with Global HR teams to strengthen HR compliance controls and risk frameworks aligned with firm risk appetite.
Ensure HR risk monitoring frameworks remain effective, scalable, and responsive to regulatory changes and business needs.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, research summaries, and guidance materials related to HR risk operations and emerging trends.
Lead HR risk management priorities and develop practical short- and long-term solutions for complex business challenges.
Serve as an escalation point for client-related onboarding, background investigation matters, and contract review.
Collaborate with ICS functions, including Finance and Payroll, to improve operational consistency and advance risk management priorities.
Provide day-to-day work direction to global data analytics team members supporting HR risk operations.

Policy Governance

Own the development, implementation, maintenance, and governance of employment policies.
Serve as a policy consultation resource for People Experience, Legal, Compliance, HRIS, Payroll, Finance, and business stakeholders.
Provide practical guidance on employment policy interpretation, process application, and risk mitigation.
Partner with Legal and Compliance to align policies with global requirements and firm standards.
Drive policy harmonization across multinational firms, acquired entities, and evolving business models.
Draft employee-facing policy communications, FAQs, and intranet content to support consistent understanding and application.

Training & Operational Excellence

Monitor emerging labor and employment laws impacting firm policies; translate legal and business changes into practical process improvements and controls.
Develop and manage firmwide HR compliance training programs, including planning, stakeholder coordination, deployment, tracking, and continuous improvement.
Deliver internal training that addresses identified compliance risks, strengthens risk mitigation practices, and promotes a culture of compliance.
Support execution of the P&C strategic plan by advancing operational excellence initiatives aligned with industry standards and business priorities.
Recommend remediation actions, process improvements, and control enhancements based on audit results, monitoring findings, and identified risk trends.
Manage AI-related HR risks by applying firm governance, monitoring regulatory developments, and refining guidelines to support compliant and responsible use.

HR Workforce Analytics, Risk Strategy & Workforce Management

Develop and maintain dashboards, trackers, heat maps, and reporting tools to monitor HR risk, compliance activity, workforce trends, and program effectiveness.
Analyze workforce and operational data to identify trends, emerging risks, control gaps, and opportunities for automation or process improvement.
Prepare executive-ready summaries, insights, recommendations, and status updates to support leadership review and decision-making.
Partner with HRIS, Technology, and analytics teams to improve data quality, reporting processes, automation, and integration of risk operations tools.
Identify and implement automation and reporting enhancements using Power Automate, Power Query, Power BI, and related tools.
Conduct adverse impact analyses as requested and summarize findings for leadership review.
Build automated tracking and reporting tools that integrate multiple data sources, streamline workflows, improve data integrity, and enable real-time reporting.

Health & Safety

Oversee management of health and safety procedures and policies, including infectious disease and workplace violence safety programs
Monitor ongoing regulatory updates including OSHA standards, injury and illness prevention programs and government contractor compliance
Assist with real-time response during crisis matters such as natural disasters, including drafting employee-facing communications and compiling resources for impacted employees

The ideal candidate will be:

A business‑minded HR Risk &Compliance professional who excels at statistical workplace analysis, internal/external HR compliance, project and process management with impeccable planning, coordination, and follow‑through.
Operationally rigorous, detail‑accurate, and deadline‑reliable in a fast‑moving, matrixed environment.
Analytical, comfortable with metrics and translating data into clear executive summaries , timelines, and stakeholder guidance.
A concise, audience‑aware communicator who can write, edit, and sequence communications that drive clarity and action.
A strong collaborator across Legal/Compliance, People & Culture, Technology/HRIS, People Experience and Inclusion teams; adept at role clarity and RACI management.
Comfortable and integrity driven professional with experience in handling highly confidential information, sound judgment, and executive‑facing professionalism.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess:

6–8 years of progressive experience in HR Compliance, HR program management, PMO/operations, or organizational effectiveness (professional services experience a plus).
Hands‑on experience building and managing complex program plans (e.g., Smartsheet), SOPs, process documentation, and trainings.
Advanced data and reporting skills (Excel/Power BI or similar) Experience with Power Queries, look-ups, pivot tables and experience supporting various systems
Proficiency with MS Office, SharePoint/Teams, and content maintenance on intranet site.
Strong written and verbal communication; experience drafting broad‑reach communications, policies, FAQs, research papers and leader talking points and briefings.
HR regulatory reporting experience
People management experience preferred.

jobs.title: Junior Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Braun Management addresses structural friction within executive teams to resolve organizational problems that have become too internal to fix. We provide rigorous analysis and evidence-backed conclusions to help leadership teams navigate complex governance and clarify decision rights.

The role

As a Junior Research Analyst, you will support our consulting team by gathering and organizing the data necessary for high-stakes executive engagements. Our partner is a Mediterranean technology firm, and much of your work will focus on assisting them with structural adjustments and market entry challenges. This role exists to ensure that our recommendations are grounded in accurate, verified information rather than intuition or generic advice. Because we operate as a fully remote team, your ability to conduct independent research and document your findings clearly is essential.

What you will do
Conducting background research on industry trends and specific company structures to identify points of organizational friction.
Compiling data reports that help our consultants understand how decision rights are currently distributed within client organizations.
Assisting in the preparation of written documentation that outlines evidence-backed paths forward for executive leadership.
Reviewing regulatory environments and governance requirements that impact our partner firm operations.
Organizing internal databases to ensure that qualitative interviews and quantitative data are easily accessible to the team.
Drafting summaries of complex business systems to help clarify where internal accountability has broken down.
Monitoring news and updates related to our specific client engagements to keep the team informed of external shifts.
Supporting the senior consultants in verifying historical performance data and organizational charts.

What we are looking for
A strong interest in understanding how complex business systems and corporate governance function in practice.
The ability to write clearly and concisely without relying on filler or corporate jargon.
High attention to detail when cross-referencing data points and verifying the accuracy of research materials.
Familiarity with basic research methodologies, perhaps gained through university projects or recent internships.
Comfort working in a remote environment where communication relies heavily on written updates and documentation.
A logical approach to problem-solving and a preference for evidence over speculation.
Willingness to learn about European governance structures and the specific challenges of organizational restructuring.
Professionalism and the ability to handle sensitive corporate information with discretion.

How we work

Braun Management operates entirely without physical offices, valuing the focus and precision that a remote setting allows. Our culture is built on written clarity and rigorous thinking, meaning we spend less time in meetings and more time producing high-quality analysis. We believe that accountability is better served by clear documentation than by constant verbal check-ins. Every team member is expected to contribute to a culture of honesty, where we address difficult structural truths directly to help our clients move forward. This remote structure requires self-discipline and a commitment to maintaining high standards of work without direct, in-person supervision.

What we offer
A permanent, full-time position that is 100 percent remote.
Competitive pay that is attractive for an entry-level role in the consulting and research sector.
Exposure to high-level organizational challenges and executive decision-making processes.
A work environment that prioritizes clear communication and evidence-backed results over office politics.
Paid time off and flexible scheduling within a results-oriented framework.
The opportunity to work with a Mediterranean technology firm on its expansion and structural growth.

In this role, your research will become the foundation for the difficult conversations our consultants have with executive leadership. By uncovering the structural truths that hinder growth, you help provide the clarity needed for organizations to reform their decision rights. Your work directly contributes to providing a clear, written path forward for the firms we serve.

Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family.

Job Summary

Within SHI, the Spend Optimization Services (SOS) organization is transforming how customers manage and optimize technology investments by connecting strategy, financial accountability, and operational execution to deliver measurable business outcomes.

The Sr. Program Analyst - Transformation supports the execution and continuous improvement of the Revenue Intelligence portfolio while contributing to broader transformation initiatives across the organization. This role partners with technical development teams, business stakeholders, and leadership to translate business needs into actionable requirements, manage delivery workflows, and drive operational excellence.

While primarily focused on the Revenue Intelligence development lifecycle, this position will also support go-to-market (GTM) initiatives, service lifecycle efforts, organizational communications, and other strategic programs as business priorities evolve.

Role Description

Lead stakeholder workshops and working sessions across Spend Optimization Services (SOS) to gather business requirements, KPI definitions, thresholds, continuous improvement opportunities, and business rules; translate findings into user stories, acceptance criteria, and prioritized backlog items.
Partner with development and business teams to refine requirements, support execution efforts, and maintain traceability from requirements through delivery to measurable business outcomes.
Develop and maintain project plans across SOS initiatives while tracking roadmap priorities, milestones, delivery commitments, cross-functional dependencies, and intake evaluation and prioritization activities.
Execute and help scale the Revenue Intelligence operating model, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, prioritization sessions, mid-sprint reviews, demonstrations, and release readiness coordination.
Apply consistent delivery practices across SOS initiatives and identify opportunities to standardize and improve execution models across teams.
Own execution tooling and delivery governance through Asana, ensuring work is prioritized, visible, measurable, and aligned with strategic objectives across Revenue Intelligence and Spend Optimization Services.
Track and manage risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, GTM launch readiness, and service lifecycle risks across multiple concurrent initiatives. Provide structured status updates, escalate blockers, and ensure alignment across teams.
Support dashboards, scorecards, and reporting tools while aligning KPI definitions across Revenue Intelligence, go-to-market intake processes, and transformation initiatives. Develop and support internal communications for Revenue Intelligence initiatives and releases, GTM launches and updates, and service offering or lifecycle changes. Create executive-ready status updates, summaries, announcements, release notes, enablement materials, stakeholder communications, newsletters, and internal briefings.
Ensure messaging is clear, consistent, strategically aligned, and tailored to leadership, sales, and delivery audiences. Partner with stakeholders to improve transparency, awareness, adoption, and change reinforcement for new tools, processes, and capabilities.

Business Analysis: Translate business needs into structured requirements and user stories
Project / Program Management: Manage multiple concurrent initiatives across analytics, GTM, and service domains
Process Design & Lifecycle Thinking: Understand and improve end-to-end service lifecycle processes
Go-to-Market Awareness: Familiarity with enablement, pipeline tracking, and launch coordination
Data & Analytical Thinking: Comfort working with KPIs, dashboards, and performance metrics
Organizational Communication: Ability to distill complex initiatives into clear, concise messaging for different audiences
Tooling & Systems: Experience with Asana (preferred) and reporting tools (Power BI, Tableau, Excel)
Communication & Facilitation: Strong workshop facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills
Adaptability & Prioritization: Evaluate competing priorities and provide structured recommendations supported by data, business context, and stakeholder input
Change Management: Ability to drive meaningful change through influence

Skill Level Requirements

Business analysis and requirements gathering.
Ability to translate business needs into structured requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Program and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives.
Process design and service lifecycle management capabilities.
Knowledge of agile or iterative delivery methodologies.
Go-to-market awareness, including enablement, pipeline tracking, launch coordination, and campaign execution.
Strong analytical skills with experience working with KPIs, dashboards, scorecards, and performance metrics.
Organizational communication skills with the ability to simplify complex initiatives for a variety of audiences.
Strong stakeholder engagement, workshop facilitation, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Ability to evaluate competing priorities and provide structured recommendations supported by data, business context, and stakeholder input.
Change management and organizational influence capabilities.
Experience supporting application development, business intelligence, transformation, and service lifecycle initiatives.
Experience creating executive communications, stakeholder-facing summaries, enablement materials, and release communications.
Experience using project delivery, collaboration, and reporting tools.
Ability to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.

Other Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.
5-7 years of experience in project coordination, program management, business analysis, transformation, or related roles.
Experience supporting cross-functional transformation initiatives involving technical, business, and leadership stakeholders to align priorities, clarify requirements, coordinate execution, and deliver measurable outcomes.
Experience supporting application development or business intelligence teams.
Experience supporting go-to-market initiatives, including sales enablement, launches, and campaign execution.
Experience supporting service or product lifecycle management activities.
Background in consulting, IT services, or transformation programs.
Ability to travel up to 5-10% for industry conferences and SHI, partner, and customer events.

Preferred

Experience with Asana administration or advanced use.
Experience with reporting and analytics tools such as Power BI, Tableau, and Excel.

The level III position will be assigned less complex projects commensurate with level of experience and will be guided by senior level Project Managers. Projects assigned will progress in complexity to enable progression to the next level.

Responsibilities Include

Reviewing Project documents for clarity and completeness - examples include scope documents, project plan, contracts, equipment and construction bid packages, requisitions, Bills of Material or Material Requests for Issue, Task Authorizations, and Engineering Work Requests.
Reviewing Project and contract budgets for adequacy and completeness. Initiating and ensuring budget revisions made and documented when required.
Ensuring change management protocols are followed to ensure complete documentation for changes in scope, schedule and costs.
Providing project status reports. Recurring, standard reports and ad hoc reports that address status of scope, budget and schedule and that identifies risks and issues and outlines mitigation strategy.
Obtaining concurrence (or buy-in) from affected departments to support the proposed schedule and resource requirements. Review and approval of Project Plans.
Validating project estimates including contingency.
Developing, with input of project team, the strategic and tactical execution plan for the project.
Monitoring and / or reporting contractor resource levels.
Ensuring adequacy of Project Team membership and participation. Responsible for overseeing the activities of consultants and contractors assigned.

Responsible for the quality assurance and control program, including identification of quality requirements, responsibility for QA program (Energy Delivery's or Contractor's program) and if required, review and approval process for contractor provided procedures.
Communicating Project goals, priorities and decisions to the Region/Corporate Leadership Team.
Ensuring Project challenge meetings, peer reviews and assessments are performed.
Working with Project Controls to develop and update the Project schedule.
Identifying and notifying the Project Team of additional resources or requirements necessary to meet the Project scope or schedule
Ensuring the close-out and lessons-learned protocols are completed. Participating in audit of completed projects to evaluate whether identified objectives and benefits have been realized.

An employee hired at the Transmission Project Manager IV level will be expected to perform all of the above responsibilities with more proficiency, and in a more independent manner. Further, the Transmission Project Manager IV level employee will be assigned additional responsibilities related to those above, including:

The level IV employee will be assigned projects of increasing complexity. Experience with project management tools such as Primavera, MS Project, etc. with related Scheduling / Resource Planning expertise is preferred.
Excellent interpersonal skills, strong written and verbal communication skills and strong analytical ability are required.
Successful candidate must be a team player and possess a willingness to work in a team environment.
Must be willing to travel to assigned project locations throughout the service territory.

Qualifications at the Transmission Project Manager IV level include all the above plus:

Related experience includes project organization, engineering, finance, construction, project management, planning or project controls.
